slides.title: Safety Philosophy
slides.description:
All injuries can be prevented or greatly reduced, all employees including managers and owners are responsible for preventing occupational injuries and illnesses.

Every effort must be made to safeguard all operating conditions that may potentially injured technicians, mechanics and other shop personnel (as well as customers and visitors) or damage property and equipment.

Learning to work and behave safely is an on-going and important part of your shop’s operation.

Working safely is the only right way of operating a shop. In the long run, it is also more cost-effective.

Accidents are caused by unsafe conditions and/or unsafe behaviors.

slides.title: Types of Unsafe Conditions and Behavior in the Shop
slides.description:
Improper rails and machine guarding

Improper lighting and ventilation

Hazardous protective equipment or apparel

Defective tools, machines, and working surfaces

Failure to used proper PPE (Personal Protective Equipment)

Unsafe positions and postures including loading, carrying and lifting

Using unsafe equipment, using equipment unsafely and making safety devices inoperative.

Moving dangerous equipment without proper training/help

Operating equipment without authority and or operating at unsafe speeds

Failure to secure objects, use lockout procedures and warn others or give proper signals

Distractions and or Horseplay

slides.title: The Cost of Accidents
slides.description:
Obviously, the injury or death of a fellow worker is costly in terms of the loss of human life or productivity of the person and to his/her family.

Out of 2 million U.S. heavy-duty and automotive-maintenance mechanics and technicians, OSHA recorded 168 fatalities and 32,000 lost-day injuries in 1996. The American Medical Association estimated in 1995 that a serious accident cost an average of $63,000. Maintaining a safe and accident-free shop adds to the shop’s profit-benefiting everyone.

slides.title: Basic Shop Safety Rules
slides.description:
Keep your work area clean

Neatly arrange equipment and material. Do not allow parts, metal, wires, scrapes or small material to accumulate on the shop floor or in your work areas. Place drink cups, cans, bottles, paper, lunch scraps, etc. in the proper containers.

Report every injuryto your supervisor, no matter how slight or insignificant the injury may seem.

Request assistance from your supervisor if you are insure about the safe operation or process of the job.

Report un-safe conditionsto your supervisor immediately. Rely on your judgment and knowledge of safety to guide you.

Horseplay is forbidden do not interfere with co-workers when they are performing their job, no running except in emergencies.

Be certain all safety guards are in place before operating any machine or equipment.

Check for the safety and clearance of all personnel before energizing or operating any machine hoist or other equipment.

All equipment must be locked out prior to any repairs or maintenance. Lock Outs my only be removed by authorized personnel/management.

Never work on an electrical system under unsafe conditions.

Pull the switch controlling the machine insuring it’s turned off. Allow equipment to come to full stop and then lock and tag it. Push start button insuring the machine is definitely off.

Never tie down, block outor otherwise make inoperative any type of safety device, attachment, method or guard.

Observe all caution and danger signs

Never oil, remove guards or attempt to repairmachinery while it is in motion. Do not climb on machinery while oiling or greasing.

Do not use electrical equipmentwhile standing in damp or wet surfaced or when your hands are wet.

Only electricians or authorized personnelare permitted to perform electrical work.

PPE required in each shop must be wornas specified. Safety-toe shoes, bump hats, safety glasses with sideshields, goggles, faceshields, respirators and other forms of protective equipment or clothing are for employee protection.

Gloves should not be wornwhen operating drills, lathes or other types of machinery that contain rotating spindles or cutting tools

Wear clothes that are suitable for work

Working without shirts is not permitted. Long-sleeve shirts must be worn when burning, welding, grinding or performing other types of work where sparks or hot metal are present, acids or similar substances.

Neckties, rings, watches and loose or ragged clothingcreate hazards. Do not wear.

Lift objects with your legs not your backs. Keep backs straight.

Observe “No Smoking Areas”

Never smoke near the following: compressed gas cylinders (oxygen-gas). Paint operation, flammable storage rooms, near gasoline or fuel stations etc.

Wipe up immediately any oil spills, grease, paintor any other slippery substance to prevent a fall.

Approved safety cans must be used for flammable liquids such as gasoline, solvents and thinners.

Know where your fire extinguishers are located.In case of a fire first pull the fire alarm.

Never use an air hose for cleaning yourself off. (psi)Approved safety guns must not exceed 30

Stay clear of objects being moved or handled by any type of conveyance when storing material.or handled by any type of conveyance when storing material.

Wear seat beltswhen driving any vehicle.

Compressed oxygen and gas cylindersmust be properly secured at all times. Caps must be installed when not in use. Only lift cylinders in approved racks or cages. Never use cylinders as rollers and keep a shutoff wrench on each acetylene cylinder that is not equipped with a valve.

Clamp or secure equipmentor material to prevent it from shifting or rotating when drilling, grinding and operating a lathe, etc.

Employees when long hair must always tie their hairback or tucked under their bump cap. This prevents your hair from being caught in any rotating machinery or parts.

Never work on a tire with a rim attached to it without first placing the tire in a protective tire cage or using a chain to secure the rim to the tire.

Never remove a taglabeled “Caution,” “Danger,” etc. without authorization. Safety tags are to be in place on air-hoist controls.

Never use an air hose to blow dustfrom brake drums, brake shoes or other brake parts. Use an approved high-efficiency particle air (HEPA) vacuum device or wet-wash method.

Work trousers should be cufflessand extended over shoes to prevent sparks from entering shoe.

Follow equipment operatingguidelines provided by manufacturer.

Follow facility guidelines for storage and handling of used oil, antifreeze, refrigerants and wastes.

Follow safe procedures when attempting to fill an in-ground lift. First depresserize the lift. Never place any part of your body over the fill plug. Use lift plugs that contain bleeder screws.

The safety rules for your dealership and your facility may be stricter than and may differ from the safety recommendations and tips given in these guidelines. Always follow the safety rules for your location. If you have any questions as to the correct safety practice, do not hesitate to ask your supervisor.
